questions.q: Why does Bellhaven run a planned failover test instead of just trusting the AG's configuration?
options: A DBA who has never watched a failover actually happen only knows it was configured to work, not that it does — an untested plan is still theoretical
SQL Server requires a manual test before automatic failover can ever be enabled
Planned failovers are required monthly by Microsoft licensing
There's no real reason — it's just a best practice with no concrete justification
questions.explain: The lesson draws the same conclusion Chapter 8 makes about DR runbooks: an HA/DR plan that has never actually been executed hasn't been proven.

questions.q: Why is ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP AG_Bellhaven FAILOVER (without FORCE) the correct command for this test?
options: SQLPRD01 and SQLPRD02 are both synchronous and currently healthy/synchronized, so this is a planned failover with no data loss
The FORCE clause is required for every failover, planned or not
FAILOVER without FORCE only works on asynchronous replicas
There is no difference between FAILOVER and FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS
questions.explain: Between healthy synchronous replicas, a plain FAILOVER is a safe, no-data-loss operation — forcing it would be reserved for a genuinely different, degraded scenario.

questions.q: What does sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states let the team confirm after the failover?
options: Each replica's current role (primary/secondary) and health, confirming SQLPRD02 actually became primary
The exact RPO in minutes for the last transaction
Which backup job ran most recently
The physical location of each replica's server
questions.explain: This DMV reports role and synchronization health per replica — the first thing to check after a failover.

questions.q: Why does the test also check that BHFS-AGL (the listener) is reachable, rather than just checking the database's role?
options: The listener is what applications actually connect through — confirming it routes to the new primary proves the failover is transparent to real client connections
The listener has no functional purpose and is only checked for documentation
The listener must be manually recreated after every failover
Applications always connect directly to SQLPRD01 regardless of the listener
questions.explain: The listener is the actual mechanism that makes failover invisible to applications — verifying it confirms the whole chain, not just the database engine's internal state.

questions.q: What does 'failing back' to SQLPRD01 involve, once the test is verified?
options: Running the identical FAILOVER command in the opposite direction, on SQLPRD01 — a routine operation between healthy synchronous partners
Rebuilding AG_Bellhaven completely from scratch
Restoring the full backup from Lesson 43 onto SQLPRD01
Failback is not possible once a failover has occurred
questions.explain: Because the pair is synchronous and symmetric, failing back is just running FAILOVER again, targeting SQLPRD01 — not a special or risky operation.
